# 1 Kings Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** King Ben-hadad of Aram mobilized his entire army. With thirty-two allied kings and their horses and chariots, he marched against Samaria and laid siege to it.
**2** He sent messengers into the city to King Ahab of Israel with this message:
**3** "Ben-hadad says: 'Your silver and gold belong to me. Your best wives and finest children belong to me.'"
**4** The king of Israel replied, "Just as you say, my lord the king — I and everything I have are yours."
**5** But the messengers returned with another demand: "Ben-hadad says: 'I sent you my first demand about your silver, gold, wives, and children.
**6** But tomorrow at this time I'm sending my officials to search your palace and the homes of your officials. They will seize whatever they find valuable and take it.'"
**7** The king of Israel summoned all the elders and said, "Look at the trouble this man is causing! He demanded my wives, children, silver, and gold, and I agreed. Now he wants to ransack our houses!"
**8** The elders and the people all said, "Don't give in. Don't agree."
**9** So Ahab told Ben-hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king: I will do everything you demanded the first time, but this latest demand I cannot accept." The messengers left with his answer.
**10** Ben-hadad sent back this threat: "May the gods strike me dead if there's enough rubble left in Samaria for each of my soldiers to grab a handful!"
**11** The king of Israel shot back, "Tell him: a soldier putting on his armor shouldn't brag like one taking it off."
**12** Ben-hadad received this message while drinking with the kings in their field headquarters. He ordered his men, "Get into position!" And they prepared to attack the city.
**13** Meanwhile, a prophet approached King Ahab and said, "This is what the LORD says: 'Do you see this massive army? I am going to hand it over to you today. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"
**14** "Through whom?" Ahab asked. The prophet answered, "The LORD says: 'Through the junior officers of the provincial commanders.'" Ahab asked, "Who starts the attack?" The prophet said, "You do."
**15** Ahab mustered the junior officers — 232 men — and behind them the full Israelite force of 7,000.
**16** They marched out at noon. Ben-hadad and the thirty-two allied kings were getting drunk in their tents.
**17** The junior officers went out first. Ben-hadad's scouts reported, "Men are coming out of Samaria."
**18** He said, "Whether they come in peace or war — take them alive."
**19** The junior officers led the charge out of the city, with the army behind them.
**20** Each man cut down his opponent. The Arameans fled, with Israel in pursuit. Ben-hadad escaped on horseback with some cavalry.
**21** The king of Israel attacked and destroyed the horses and chariots, inflicting massive casualties on the Arameans.
**22** Afterward the prophet warned Ahab, "Regroup and prepare. The king of Aram will attack again next spring."
**23** Ben-hadad's advisers told him, "Their god is a god of the hills — that's why they beat us. But if we fight them on flat ground, we'll win.
**24** Here's what you should do: replace the kings with professional commanders.
**25** Rebuild your army to match what you lost — same number of troops, horses, and chariots. Then we'll fight them on the plains and crush them." He took their advice.
**26** The following spring, Ben-hadad mustered the Aramean army and marched to Aphek to fight Israel.
**27** Israel also mobilized and marched out to meet them. The Israelites looked like two small flocks of goats compared to the Arameans, who covered the landscape.
**28** A man of God approached the king of Israel and said, "The LORD says: 'Because the Arameans think the LORD is only a god of the hills and not of the valleys, I will hand this entire army over to you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.'"
**29** For seven days the two armies camped facing each other. On the seventh day, battle was joined. The Israelites killed 100,000 Aramean foot soldiers in a single day.
**30** The survivors fled into the city of Aphek, where the city wall collapsed on 27,000 of them. Ben-hadad escaped into the city and hid in an inner room.
**31** His officials said, "We've heard that the kings of Israel are merciful. Let's put on sackcloth and ropes and go to the king of Israel. Maybe he'll spare your life."
**32** Wearing sackcloth around their waists and ropes on their heads, they went to the king of Israel. "Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please let me live,'" they said. Ahab replied, "He's still alive? He's my brother!"
**33** The men seized on that word immediately. "Yes — your brother Ben-hadad!" they said. "Go get him," said Ahab. Ben-hadad came out, and Ahab had him climb up into his own chariot.
**34** Ben-hadad offered, "I'll return the cities my father took from your father. You may set up trade markets in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." "On those terms, I'll release you," Ahab said. He made a treaty with him and let him go.
**35** One of the members of a prophetic guild told a fellow prophet, by the LORD's command, "Hit me!" But the man refused.
**36** So the prophet said, "Because you disobeyed the LORD, a lion will kill you as soon as you leave me." And when the man walked away, a lion found him and killed him.
**37** The prophet found someone else and said, "Hit me!" This man struck him and wounded him.
**38** The prophet then went and waited for the king along the road, disguised with a bandage over his eyes.
**39** As the king passed by, the prophet called out, "Your Majesty, I was in the thick of battle when a soldier brought me a prisoner and said, 'Guard this man. If he escapes, you'll pay with your life — or a talent of silver.'
**40** But while I was busy with this and that, the prisoner disappeared." The king of Israel said, "That's your own verdict. You've pronounced your own sentence."
**41** The prophet quickly ripped the bandage off his eyes, and the king recognized him as one of the prophets.
**42** The prophet said, "This is what the LORD says: 'You set free a man I had determined should die. Therefore your life will be taken instead of his, and your people instead of his people.'"
**43** The king of Israel went home to Samaria, sullen and furious.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **20:11 — "a soldier putting on his armor shouldn't brag like one taking it off"**: Ahab's single great line. For once, the worst king in Israel says the wisest thing in the room.
2. **20:23 — "their god is a god of the hills"**: The Arameans make a theological mistake that will cost them 100,000 soldiers. They think YHWH is a local deity with geographic limitations. God takes their error personally and answers it militarily.
3. **20:31 — "the kings of Israel are merciful"**: Reputation matters. Even enemy nations know Israel's kings tend toward mercy. Whether Ahab's mercy here is virtue or weakness depends on whether the man you're releasing was under God's death sentence — which he was.
4. **20:42 — "a man I had determined should die"**: Ben-hadad was under ḥerem — the divine ban. Ahab's release of him parallels Saul's catastrophic mercy toward Agag (1 Sam 15). In both cases, a king's unauthorized compassion toward God's designated enemy becomes the king's own death sentence.

— PNEUMA
